q: Which CPU register always holds the address of the next instruction to be fetched from memory?
exp: The Program Counter (PC) stores the address of the next instruction and is updated after each fetch.

q: In the instruction ADD R1, #25, the second operand is specified using which addressing mode?
exp: The '#' indicates that the constant 25 is part of the instruction itself, which is immediate addressing.

q: A direct-mapped cache has a total capacity of 4 KB and a block size of 16 bytes. How many cache lines does it have?
exp: Number of lines = 4096 / 16 = 256.

q: An ideal 5-stage pipeline (no stalls) executes 100 instructions. How many clock cycles are needed in total?
In DMA, the mode in which the DMA controller takes over the bus for just one memory cycle at a time and then returns it to the CPU is called
exp: In cycle stealing the DMA controller steals single bus cycles from the CPU between its own accesses.

q: In register transfer notation, the statement P: R2 ← R1 means
options: R2 is copied into R1 whenever P equals 1
R1 and R2 are exchanged on every clock
R2 is cleared when P equals 0
R1 is copied into R2 only when the control function P equals 1
exp: The control function P gates the transfer; the content of R1 is copied to R2 and R1 is unchanged.

q: Which of the following is NOT a function of the control unit?
exp: Arithmetic and logic operations are done by the ALU; the control unit only fetches, decodes and sequences operations.

q: A 16-bit instruction has a 4-bit opcode and three register address fields of equal size. How many registers can each field address?
exp: Remaining bits = 12, so each field has 4 bits and can address 2⁴ = 16 registers.

q: Temporal locality of reference means that
options: A recently accessed item is likely to be accessed again soon
Items near a recently accessed item are likely to be accessed soon
Programs access memory only in sequential order
Data is always stored in sorted order
exp: Temporal locality is re-use of the same item in a short time; the nearby-item case is spatial locality.

q: A data hazard in which an instruction tries to read a register before a previous instruction has written its result is called
exp: This is Read After Write (RAW), a true data dependence.

q: Which type of interrupt cannot be disabled (masked) by the processor?
exp: A non-maskable interrupt (NMI) is always serviced; used for critical events such as power failure.

q: In a Hamming error-correcting code, the parity check bits are placed at bit positions
options: the last p positions of the word
exp: Check bit P(2^k) at position 2^k covers all positions whose binary representation has bit k set; the syndrome then gives the error position.

q: What is the range of integers that can be represented in 8-bit two's complement form?
exp: n-bit two's complement range is -2^(n-1) to 2^(n-1) - 1, i.e. -128 to +127.

q: In the checksum method with 1's-complement addition, the receiver finds no error when the 1's-complement sum of all words including the checksum is
options: equal to the first data word
exp: The sender sends the complement of the sum, so the receiver's sum becomes all 1s (whose complement is 0) if there is no error.

q: The cache is accessed first (10 ns) and, on a miss, main memory is then accessed (additional 100 ns). With a hit ratio of 0.9, the average memory access time is
exp: AMAT = hit time + miss rate × miss penalty = 10 + 0.1 × 100 = 20 ns.

q: Which of the following is a characteristic of a RISC processor?
options: Variable-length instructions with many memory-to-memory operations
A very large number of addressing modes
exp: RISC uses simple fixed-length instructions and only load/store instructions access memory.

q: A CPU has a 16-bit address bus. What is the maximum amount of memory it can directly address?
exp: 2¹⁶ = 65536 locations = 64 KB (for byte addressing).

q: In Flynn's classification, a machine with one control unit that broadcasts the same instruction to many processing elements, each working on its own data, is
exp: Single Instruction stream, Multiple Data streams (SIMD), e.g. array and vector processors.

q: Which CPU register is used to hold intermediate results of ALU operations in a simple one-address machine?
exp: The accumulator holds one operand and receives the ALU result.

q: Zero-address instructions are characteristic of which type of machine organization?
exp: Stack machines take operands implicitly from the top of the stack, so arithmetic instructions need no address field.

q: A page fault occurs when
options: The CPU tries to write to read-only memory
A required block is not found in the cache
The referenced page is not present in main memory
exp: A page fault is raised when the page needed is not resident in main memory and must be brought in from disk.

q: A non-pipelined unit takes 50 ns per instruction. A 5-stage pipeline with 10 ns stages executes 100 instructions. The speedup obtained is approximately
exp: Non-pipelined = 100 × 50 = 5000 ns; pipelined = (5 + 99) × 10 = 1040 ns; speedup = 5000/1040 ≈ 4.81.

q: In programmed I/O, the CPU repeatedly checking the status register of a device until it is ready is called
exp: Repeatedly testing device status in a loop (busy waiting) is polling.

q: The micro-operation R3 ← R1 + R2' + 1 (R2' = 1's complement of R2) performs
exp: R2' + 1 is the 2's complement (negative) of R2, so the sum is R1 − R2.

q: In a microprogrammed control unit, the microinstructions are stored in
exp: Microprograms reside in a special, usually ROM, control memory.

q: A branch instruction uses PC-relative addressing. The PC (already incremented) holds 1000 and the offset field is +24. The effective address is
exp: Effective address = PC + offset = 1000 + 24 = 1024.

q: Which cache mapping technique needs no replacement algorithm because each memory block maps to exactly one line?
exp: In direct mapping a block has a single possible line, so there is no choice of victim.

q:
Statement I: RISC processors typically use hardwired control. Statement II: CISC processors commonly use microprogrammed control.
Which is correct?
exp: Simple RISC instruction sets allow fast hardwired control, whereas complex CISC instruction sets are usually implemented with microprograms.

q: Daisy chaining in an interrupt system is used for
options: Resolving priority among several interrupting devices
exp: Devices are connected in series; the one nearest the CPU gets the highest priority.

q: Why must a DRAM be refreshed periodically?
options: Its flip-flops lose state when the clock stops
The charge stored on its capacitors leaks away
exp: A DRAM cell is one transistor plus a capacitor; leakage means every row must be rewritten every few milliseconds. SRAM flip-flops need no refresh.

q: To set to 1 only those bits of register A where register B has 1s, leaving the other bits of A unchanged, the micro-operation is
exp: OR with 1 gives 1, OR with 0 leaves the bit unchanged (selective-set). XOR toggles and AND clears.

q: The correct sequence of the basic instruction cycle is
exp: An instruction is fetched, then decoded, then executed.

q: Which of the following has the smallest access time?
exp: Registers sit inside the CPU and are the fastest level of the memory hierarchy.

q: A structural hazard in a pipeline arises when
options: Two instructions need the same hardware resource in the same cycle
An instruction depends on the result of a previous one
A branch changes the program counter
exp: Structural hazards are resource conflicts, e.g. a single memory port needed by both instruction fetch and data access.

q: In memory-mapped I/O,
options: Special IN and OUT instructions are mandatory
I/O devices have a completely separate address space
I/O devices can only be used through DMA
Device registers share the memory address space and are accessed using ordinary load/store instructions
exp: Memory-mapped I/O assigns addresses from the memory space to device registers, so normal memory instructions work.

q: A program has 80% of its execution time parallelizable. By Amdahl's law the speedup on 4 processors is
Which type of control unit is generally faster but less flexible to modify?
exp: A hardwired control unit uses fixed logic circuits, so it is faster but harder to change than a microprogrammed one.

q: The address field of an instruction is 500 and the index register contains 25. Using indexed addressing, the effective address is
exp: Effective address = address field + index register = 500 + 25 = 525.

q: Which cache write policy updates both the cache and main memory on every write hit?
exp: Write-through writes to the cache and to memory simultaneously, keeping memory always consistent.

q: A Translation Lookaside Buffer (TLB) is
options: A register file for floating-point numbers
A small fast cache holding recently used page-table entries
exp: The TLB caches recent virtual-to-physical translations to avoid a page-table access in memory.
